summary: Core software components needed to build AI agents: LLM provider, UI/interface, tool system, and orchestrator

content.overview: Building an AI agent requires four fundamental software components: (1) LLM Provider (the reasoning engine), (2) UI/Interface (user interaction layer), (3) Tool System (external capabilities), and (4) Orchestrator (coordinates components and manages conversation flow). Unlike design patterns (ReAct, Reflection), this is the concrete SOFTWARE architecture - the components you must implement or integrate to build a functioning agent.
keyPoints: LLM Provider: Core reasoning engine - handles prompt processing, response generation, streaming. Must support: API integration, token management, model selection, error handling
UI/Interface Layer: User interaction - can be CLI, web UI (Blazor, React), API endpoints, or chat interface. Handles: user input, response display, conversation history, real-time streaming

Tool System: External capabilities - enables agent to act beyond text generation. Includes: tool registration, parameter validation, execution, result handling. Common tools: file access, web search, API calls, database queries
Orchestrator: Coordinates all components - manages conversation flow, routes requests to LLM, executes tool calls, maintains state, handles errors. The 'brain' that connects UI → LLM → Tools
CRITICAL: Orchestrator is the glue - it implements the agent loop: receive user input → send to LLM → parse tool calls → execute tools → send results to LLM → return to user
State Management: Conversation history, tool call logs, user preferences - must persist across sessions and handle concurrent conversations
Configuration: API keys, model selection, tool permissions, UI settings - externalize via environment variables or config files (NEVER hardcode)
Error Handling: LLM failures, tool errors, network issues - implement retry logic, graceful degradation, user-friendly error messages

examples.title: Basic Agent Architecture Stack
examples.code:
// Component layers:

[UI Layer] → Blazor/React/CLI
     ↓
[Orchestrator] → AgentOrchestrator
     ↓ (prompts)        ↓ (tool calls)
[LLM Provider]    [Tool System]
     ↓ (responses)      ↓ (results)
[Orchestrator] ← combines results
     ↓
[UI Layer] ← displays to user
examples.explanation: The orchestrator sits between UI and execution layers, routing requests and coordinating responses

examples.title: Orchestrator Core Loop
examples.explanation: Orchestrator manages the conversation loop, delegating to LLM and tools as needed

warnings: NEVER tightly couple components - use abstraction layers (interfaces) so you can swap LLM providers, UIs, or tools without rewriting the orchestrator
State management is critical - losing conversation history mid-session breaks agent continuity and user experience
Tool execution can be dangerous - ALWAYS validate inputs, implement permissions, sandbox execution for untrusted tools
Streaming responses improve UX but complicate error handling - tools can't be executed until LLM finishes streaming, requires careful buffering
Configuration sprawl - as agents grow, config becomes complex. Use structured config (JSON/YAML) with validation, not scattered env vars
Cost tracking - LLM API calls accumulate fast. Log token usage, implement budgets, cache repeated queries where safe
bestPractices: Design for modularity: Define clear interfaces (ILLMProvider, IToolSystem, IOrchestrator) to enable component swapping
Implement transparency: Log all LLM prompts, responses, tool calls, and results - critical for debugging and user trust
Handle failures gracefully: LLM timeouts, tool errors, network issues - implement retry logic, fallbacks, user-friendly error messages
Persist conversation state: Store history in database or session storage - enables conversation resumption, audit trails, analytics
Configuration hierarchy: Environment variables (secrets) → config files (settings) → defaults (fallbacks) - NEVER commit secrets
Start simple, add complexity incrementally: Basic orchestrator → add streaming → add multi-agent → add reflection patterns
